newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan shares slide lower as Wall Street tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Milan shares slide lower as Wall Street tumbles.

text.p: Italian stocks slid to a lower close on Friday depressed by the sharp fall on Wall Street, while the Italian bourse was largely unmoved by the details of the government's three-year DPEF economic plan.

Dealers said the stocks fall was largely inspired by the sharp drop in New York weighed down by a second quarter profits warning from computer chipmaker Intel, while a revised U.S. Q1 GDP figure to show a 5.8 percent rise from 5.6 percent weighed on sentiment as it pointed towards a very strong U.S. economy.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 1.23 percent at 12,087 while the Mib30 index was 1.36 percent lower at 17,966.

Dealers said that general uncertainty about the European single currency continued to weigh on the market while there was caution ahead of Sunday's run-off vote in French parliamentary elections, where the left-wing were ahead in the first round.

The DPEF produced few surprises and disappointed some who had hoped for some strong words on tackling pension reform. It outlined a 25 trillion lire 1998 deficit cutting budget while inflation and GDP forecasts were largely as expected.
One of only a few shares to rise was Italy's tyre and cables group Pirelli which ended up 2.18 percent at 3,697 lire after an analysts meeting in Milan today.

Analysts said that the Pirelli presentation would not lead to new profit estimates for this year, but it did confirm hopes for a continued rise in profitability at the company with a profit margin objective of 16 percent for 1999.
Other blue chips were off with the market, Fiat down 0.77 percent at 5,573 lire, Olivetti off 0.66 percent at 493.8 lire and Montedison 0.77 percent lower at 1,034 lire.
Oil giant ENI was off sharply, down 2.78 percent at 8,476 lire, as the market awaited the third tranche of shares to be offered by the Italian Treasury later in June.
